title: "Gateway Worker"
description: "Cloudflare Worker in front of tuturuuu.com: route manifest, Marketing page cache, web family dispatch, rollback and smoke checks."
updatedAt: "2026-11-21"
audience: developers

`apps/gateway` is a Cloudflare Worker routed on `tuturuuu.com/*`. It sends
mounted apps to their Worker bindings, serves Marketing pages from the
`apps/marketing` Worker through the Workers Cache API, and hands every Web path
to an `apps/web` family Worker over a service binding. Web has no HTTP origin:
Vercel serves no part of `tuturuuu.com`, and nothing routes traffic back to it.

The route `tuturuuu.com/*` is attached by the provider owner. Versions are
uploaded and deployed by the `gateway` job of `.github/workflows/web-opennext.yaml`
(see [Web route families](/build/devops/web-opennext-families#deploying)); more
specific routes, such as `tuturuuu.com/roadmap` and
`tuturuuu.com/roadmap/*`, take precedence over `tuturuuu.com/*` for
requests they match.

## Behavior

- **Manifest:** `apps/gateway/src/manifest.json` maps URL patterns to an origin
  and a cache class. `page` is an anonymous public page, `static` is a build or
  public asset, and anything unmatched is `bypass`. Only the `marketing` origin
  (`MARKETING_ORIGIN`) is an HTTP origin; a path whose origin is `web` goes to
  the [web families](#web-route-families) and never enters the cache. A unit
  test checks that every path in
  `apps/web/src/lib/seo/public-routes.generated.json` is a `page` route, so the
  manifest cannot drift from the marketing pages.
- **Cache:** `GET` and `HEAD` on `page` and `static` routes served by the
  Marketing origin. Fresh for 5 minutes,
  then served stale for up to 1 hour while a background refresh runs
  (`X-Gateway-Cache: HIT | STALE | MISS`). Only `200` responses without
  `Set-Cookie` and without `Vary: *` are stored. Pages vary by locale bucket
  (path prefix, then `NEXT_LOCALE`, then `Accept-Language`); `GET` and `HEAD`
  share an entry; tracking query parameters (`utm_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`,
  `msclkid`) are not part of the key.
- **Bypass:** non-`GET`/`HEAD` methods, `Authorization`, `Range`, RSC requests
  (`RSC`, `Next-Router-*`, `Next-Action` headers or `_rsc` parameter) and, for
  pages, any session-like cookie (`sb-*`, names containing `session`, `auth` or
  `token`, `tuturuuu*`, `__Secure-`/`__Host-`). Static assets ignore cookies.
  Bypassed requests are forwarded with method, headers, body and cookies
  untouched; redirects are not followed and `Set-Cookie` is returned as sent.
- **Redirects:** a Marketing `Location` that points at the Marketing origin host
  is rewritten to `PUBLIC_HOST`. Family requests already carry the public host. Marketing robots are finalized against the public ingress URL as described below.
- **Origin `Cache-Control`:** ignored on cacheable routes by default (dynamic
  Next pages send `private, no-store`). Set
  `GATEWAY_RESPECT_ORIGIN_CACHE_CONTROL=true` to honour `no-store` and
  `private`.
- **Failure:** a Web path with no bound family, including the fallback
  `web-rest` (`WEB_FAMILY_WEB_REST`), answers `503 gateway web family
  unavailable` and is never forwarded elsewhere. An unreachable Marketing
  origin answers `502`, a throwing family `502`, and a request that already
  passed through the gateway (`x-gateway-hop`) `508`.

## Configuration

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PUBLIC_HOST` | variable | Public hostname for redirect rewriting. Default `tuturuuu.com`. |
| `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX` | variable | `1` forces private robots, including cached pages. |
| `GATEWAY_MODE` | variable | Unread by the Worker. The deploy parity tooling still requires the name; there is no passthrough mode. |
| `GATEWAY_RESPECT_ORIGIN_CACHE_CONTROL` | variable | `true` honours origin `no-store`/`private`. |
| `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` | variable | Comma-separated web family ids served by their `WEB_FAMILY_<ID>` binding. Unflagged paths go to the bound `web-rest` family. |
| `WEB_ORIGIN` | unused | Never read by the Worker. The deploy config still requires it to match its live binding. |
| `TRUSTED_PROXY_ORIGIN_SECRET` | secret, required | At least 32 characters; signs the visitor IP for Web (see [Visitor IP for Web](#visitor-ip-for-web)). Equal to Web's value. |

`wrangler.jsonc` lists required secret names under `secrets.required`; the CI
deploy config (`scripts/ci/gateway-deploy-config.mjs`) refuses to deploy when
the live Worker lacks one.

## Releasing and rollback

Gateway versions are uploaded and deployed by CI as described in
[Uploading a gateway version](#vinext-family-route-table): capture the serving
version, upload, deploy at 0%, smoke with a version override, then move to
100%. After the move, run the smoke script against production:

```bash
node apps/gateway/scripts/gateway-smoke.mjs --base https://tuturuuu.com
```

It checks the Marketing pages (`200`, second request served from cache, no
`Set-Cookie` on cached responses), that Web paths and the login page answer
with `x-gateway-cache: FAMILY`, that an anonymous dashboard path redirects to
login on the public host, and that session cookies and `Authorization` go to
a family.

**Rollback** is re-assigning the previous gateway version (`wrangler rollback
<version-id> --name tuturuuu-gateway`). There is no passthrough flag and no
other origin to fall back to. No purge is needed: Marketing cache entries
expire within 65 minutes.

## Visitor IP for Web

Web family requests come from the gateway Worker, so Web rate-limiting keyed
on the calling address would block one shared address for every visitor
behind it. The gateway therefore signs the
visitor address into `x-tuturuuu-origin-auth`, which a Web runtime set to
`TRUSTED_PROXY=cloudflare-origin` verifies
(`packages/utils/src/abuse-protection/client-ip.ts`). The family Workers run
`TRUSTED_PROXY=cloudflare` and read `cf-connecting-ip` directly. Client-sent
`x-vercel-*` headers never reach a family or the Marketing origin.

- **Proof:** `hmac-v1;<unix seconds>;<ip>;<hex HMAC-SHA256>`, valid for 60
  seconds. `apps/gateway/src/origin-ip-proof.ts` signs with Web Crypto and
  matches `createOriginClientIpProof` in
  `packages/utils/src/abuse-protection/origin-ip-proof.ts` byte for byte; its
  test cross-checks both and verifies gateway proofs with the utils verifier.
- **Source address:** only the edge-set `cf-connecting-ip` of the incoming
  request. A client-sent `x-tuturuuu-origin-auth`, `X-Forwarded-For`,
  `X-Real-IP` or `True-Client-IP` never changes the signed address, and a
  client-sent proof never reaches any origin.
- **Recipients:** web family Workers (`WEB_FAMILY_*`) only. The Marketing
  origin and mounted apps (`MOUNT_*`) never receive it; none of them runs
  `cloudflare-origin`. Web family Workers run `TRUSTED_PROXY=cloudflare` and
  read `cf-connecting-ip` directly, so the proof there only keeps both paths
  alike.
- **Missing key:** without a secret of at least 32 characters, or without a
  valid `cf-connecting-ip`, the header is omitted and the isolate logs one
  warning (no value). Web then keys on `cf-connecting-ip`.

- **Calling Worker zone:** beside its proof, the gateway forwards the
  Cloudflare-set `CF-Worker` value of the incoming request in
  `x-tuturuuu-origin-worker`; a client-sent copy never passes. Web trusts it
  only with a valid proof for the same address
  (`packages/utils/src/abuse-protection/abuse-subject.ts`).
- **Shared Cloudflare addresses:** an address in Cloudflare's published ranges
  (`packages/utils/src/abuse-protection/cloudflare-ip-ranges.ts`) is never
  blocked as a unit and never earns location trust. Blocks and abuse
  escalation apply to its calling Worker zone instead. Anonymous API requests
  from it are rate-limited per Worker zone, or per client under a bounded
  aggregate for the address when no zone is named; CMS delivery reads are
  limited per site and caller (`packages/utils/src/api-proxy-limiter-subjects.ts`).
  Credentials never select a bucket before they are verified. Verified
  sessions and actors keep their own buckets, and a visitor address from a
  valid proof is keyed per IP.

Configuration, by name only:

| Where | Name | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway Worker (`tuturuuu-gateway`) | `TRUSTED_PROXY_ORIGIN_SECRET` | Worker secret, at least 32 random characters |
| Web family Workers | `TRUSTED_PROXY` | `cloudflare` |
| Web family Workers | `TRUSTED_PROXY_ORIGIN_SECRET` | The same value as the gateway secret |

Enable in this order: put the gateway secret
(`bunx wrangler secret put TRUSTED_PROXY_ORIGIN_SECRET --name tuturuuu-gateway`),
deploy the gateway, set both family Worker values and deploy the families. Confirm in Web
logs that rate-limit and block keys show visitor addresses, not Cloudflare
ranges.

**Rotation.** Web verifies one key, so change both ends back to back: put the
new gateway secret, then set the families' `TRUSTED_PROXY_ORIGIN_SECRET` and
deploy them. Until they serve the new value, proofs fail and the families key
on `cf-connecting-ip` directly. Other holders of the same origin secret, such as the
[standalone API](/build/devops/standalone-api) forwarder, rotate with it.

**Rollback.** Re-assign the previous gateway or family Worker version. Deleting the gateway secret also stops the
header, but CI gateway deploys refuse to run until it is restored or removed
from `secrets.required`.

## Local checks

```bash
cd apps/gateway
vp test
vp lint --config .oxlintrc.json src --deny-warnings
```

## Marketing page groups

The gateway serves a page group from the `apps/marketing` Worker instead of the web families. Each group is one flag.

| Group | Paths |
| --- | --- |
| `legal` | `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/acceptable-use`, `/community-guidelines`, `/security`, `/legal/*`, `/security/*` |
| `company` | `/about`, `/branding`, `/careers`, `/contact`, `/contributors`, `/partners`, `/women-in-tech` |
| `products` | `/products`, `/products/*` except `/products/meet` and `/products/meet/*` |
| `solutions` | `/solutions/*` |
| `blog` | `/blog`, `/blog/*` |
| `home` | `/`, `/pricing` |

`/changelog`, `/download`, `/models`, `/meet`, `/meet-together`, `/portfolio`, `/qr-generator`, `/visualizations/*` and the Meet product page (`/products/meet`, `/products/meet/*`, which `/meet` redirects anonymous visitors to) always stay on the web families.

Two Worker variables control the flip:

- `MARKETING_ORIGIN`: the `https://` origin of the marketing Worker. Without it, every group stays on the web families.
- `GATEWAY_MARKETING_GROUPS`: comma-separated group names served by the marketing origin, for example `legal,company`.

Flip a group by adding its name and redeploying the gateway variables. Roll it back by removing the name, or by clearing `GATEWAY_MARKETING_GROUPS`. Cached pages from the other origin are keyed separately and expire within the cache window, so a rollback is complete within one stale period.

Smoke for each group before the next one: anonymous 200 on two paths of the group, `x-gateway-cache` present, and `x-tuturuuu-runtime: native` on a cache MISS from the marketing origin.

`/assets/*` is the Vite build output of the marketing app. It always goes to `MARKETING_ORIGIN` (cached as static) and falls back to the web families while `MARKETING_ORIGIN` is unset. It is not tied to a page-group flag, so rolling a group back does not move `/assets/*`.

## Marketing robots at the gateway

Marketing groups use the shared `seo-policy.json` Marketing allowlist against
`Request.url` at gateway ingress. Only canonical HTTPS `tuturuuu.com` URLs in
an enabled Marketing page group can be public. Private, unknown, malformed and
noncanonical Marketing responses remain noindex. Forwarded host/protocol
headers are not authority for this decision. Group ownership stays literal;
decoding a path for SEO does not move it to another origin.

Responses from Web and mounted apps keep their own robots policy on the
canonical `https://tuturuuu.com` URL: Web publishes `/changelog`, `/download`,
`/models`, `/portfolio`, `/cite` and `/products/meet` in its sitemap and marks
its private routes `noindex` itself. The gateway forces those responses private
only on a noncanonical URL or under gateway `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`, and strips
any `x-marketing-origin-robots` marker from them.

Marketing's response wrapper emits `x-marketing-origin-robots: 1` only when it
adds the standard private robots header for a noncanonical backend origin and
there is no upstream robots header or explicit `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`. The gateway
can remove exactly that origin-derived restriction on an eligible public page;
it consumes the marker on every response. Unmarked upstream noindex, including
explicit private directives, stays intact. Marketing remains private when
accessed directly. Bodies, status, CSP, Vary, authentication and cookie headers
continue through the existing response path.

Gateway `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1` forces private robots even on cache hits. A backend
flag change cannot retroactively change an existing gateway cache entry: use the
gateway override when an immediate stop is required. Old unmarked cache entries
remain private until expiry or an independently authorized cache operation.

Regression coverage lives in `apps/gateway/src/marketing-robots.test.ts` and
`marketing-transport.test.ts`: rewritten backend requests, real loopback HTTP,
cache hits, redirects, explicit restrictions, and adversarial host/path inputs.
Source tests and policy fixtures do not qualify the full emitted Marketing
renderer. Before release, require exact-commit app build/type/lint/test/security
evidence, independent route/security review, emitted gateway and Marketing
Worker compatibility checks, and canonical/staging runtime header acceptance.
Provider deployment and cache operations belong to the release owner.

## Apps mounted at tuturuuu.com/&lt;app&gt;

An app can receive apex traffic through the gateway alone, or it can own zone
routes directly. A direct mount can use two zone routes on its own Worker: `tuturuuu.com/<app>` and `tuturuuu.com/<app>/*`. They
are more specific than the gateway's `tuturuuu.com/*`, so those requests never
reach the gateway. One case slips through: a zone route cannot match the bare
path once a query string is present, so `tuturuuu.com/<app>?x=1` would fall to
the gateway and on to Web.

The gateway can cover that gap through a service binding or own the complete
apex mount. Configure the paths the gateway should dispatch:

- Add the exact mount to `GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS` (comma-separated, e.g.
  `/learn,/tasks`). Add `/<app>/*` (e.g. `/learn,/learn/*`) only when the
  gateway should also hand that app its nested paths.
- Bind the app Worker as `MOUNT_<SEGMENT>` (`MOUNT_LEARN`, `MOUNT_STORE`).
  The deploy helper merges committed mount paths and services with live
  configuration. A conflicting live service target fails the deploy.

A service binding is not a same-zone subrequest, so the request reaches the
Worker directly. Only requests on `PUBLIC_HOST` mount, and
`/api` never mounts. The URL, prefix, query, method and body reach the app
unchanged. Client-supplied forwarding and framework-internal headers
(`x-forwarded-*`, `Forwarded`, `x-real-ip`, `x-original-*`, `x-rewrite-url`,
`x-middleware-*`, `x-nextjs-*`, `x-next-intl-*`, `x-tuturuuu-*`, `x-gateway-*`)
are stripped and none are synthesized, so a mounted app takes its public origin
from its own configuration. Responses carry `x-gateway-cache: MOUNT` and are
never cached by the gateway. Nested paths without a `/<app>/*` entry,
lookalikes (`/learning`) and unlisted or unbound paths go to the web families. Regression coverage lives in
`apps/gateway/src/worker-mount.test.ts`.

### Version-pinned asset smoke

Before activating any mounted app, check the candidate HTML on both its
subdomain and apex mount. Pass document URLs that should render HTML, then
save the JSON receipt with the app's other version-pinned smoke results.

```bash
python3 apps/gateway/scripts/mounted_assets_smoke.py \
  --subdomain-url "https://${APP_SUBDOMAIN}/" \
  --apex-url "https://tuturuuu.com/${APP_MOUNT}" \
  --app-worker "$APP_WORKER" --app-version "$APP_VERSION" \
  --gateway-version "$GATEWAY_VERSION"
```

The check fetches each HTTP stylesheet, module preload, script, image
(including responsive sources), font preload, manifest and icon URL declared
in the HTML. It uses the emitted URL as the browser resolves it. A redirect,
non-200 result, or HTML fallback on an asset fails the check. The version
override header goes only to the two release origins. If the check fails,
keep the candidate at 0% traffic.

### Roadmap query routing

An exact `tuturuuu.com/roadmap` zone route excludes requests such as
`/roadmap?x=1`. If they reach Web, Web's Roadmap proxy fetches the same apex URL
again and hits the loop guard. Keep the exact and subtree zone routes in
place. Add only `/roadmap` to `GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS` and bind
`MOUNT_ROADMAP` to the Roadmap Worker to handle bare requests with queries.
The exact path keeps `/roadmapping` on its existing Web route.

Check the bare path, `?x=1`, and a UTM query in English and Vietnamese.
Confirm the Roadmap version and Tech stack section on all six responses, and
check that `/roadmapping` still reaches Web. See the
[Roadmap cutover packet](/build/devops/wave1-cutover-packets#roadmap).

### One-action rollback for a gateway mount

For a new mount, keep the existing apex route and subdomain routing in place.
Admit both `/<app>` and `/<app>/*` in a single gateway version with its service
binding. Capture the route inventory and verify that no more-specific zone
route bypasses the gateway. Capture the active gateway version ID and prove
that it still serves the current paths before deploying the new version.

The gateway workflow reads bindings from the version at 100% traffic. Worker
settings can reflect a newer upload that is still at 0%. The workflow checks
the captured deployment again before upload and before sending traffic to the
new version. A changed deployment stops the run so it can use a fresh capture.

If activation changes only the gateway version, one rollback restores the
previous dispatch and bindings across its existing route:

```bash
wrangler rollback <prior-gateway-version-id> --name tuturuuu-gateway \
  --message "Restore gateway routing"
```

Rehearse this against the staging equivalents and verify the before, active
and restored request paths. Independent DNS, zone routes and target Worker
versions need separate changes, so keep them out of this activation. Mount
dispatch precedes the Web manifest. Pause gateway releases during the watch so a
rollback cannot discard another gateway change. If a rollout is reverted,
hold future gateway deploys until the mount configuration reflects that
decision.

After each switch, confirm the expected build identity twice in succession
from both watch locations before fetching any assets referenced by the live
HTML. Allow a bounded readiness interval for documented preimage responses
while the deployment reaches the edge. Roll back on an unexpected response
or if that interval expires. Start the post-deploy watch after both the app
and gateway have converged.

### Committed mount inventory and Web's active-mount list

`GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS` and the `MOUNT_*` services in `apps/gateway/wrangler.jsonc`
are the committed inventory of live mounts. Web's active-mount list
(`NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTURUUU_ACTIVE_APP_MOUNTS`) is derived from it at build time:

```bash
node scripts/active-app-mounts.mjs                        # e.g. calendar,infra,learn,...
node scripts/active-app-mounts.mjs --live <version.json>  # also require every path live
```

The script maps each mount base to its app through the shared-origin registry
(`packages/utils/src/app-mounts.ts`, aliases included), skips the session-less
`/roadmap` and `/lms`, and exits non-zero on an unregistered mount or an empty
list. Web returns a login to `/<app>/verify-token` only for listed apps, so commit
a mount only after, or in the same change as, the gateway write that makes it
live, and run the `--live` check against the captured version after that write.

### Legacy subdomain redirect

Once `tuturuuu.com/<app>` passes its smoke, the app's legacy hostname
(`<app>.tuturuuu.com`) moves to the `tuturuuu-apex-redirect` Worker
(`apps/gateway/wrangler.subdomain-redirect.jsonc`, entry
`src/subdomain-redirect-worker.ts`). Attach the hostname the same way the app
holds it: reassign its zone route `<app>.tuturuuu.com/*`, or update its Worker
custom domain to the redirect Worker. Capture the prior attachment first.

- Bind the app Worker as `APP_<APP>` (`APP_TASKS`). A hostname without a
  binding answers `404`.
- `SUBDOMAIN_REDIRECT_APPS` lists the apps whose navigations (`GET`/`HEAD`
  with `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, or `Accept: text/html` without Fetch
  Metadata) answer `301` to `https://tuturuuu.com/<app><path><query>`. The
  subdomain root maps to the bare mount.
- Everything else reaches the app Worker unchanged through its binding:
  fetches, mutations, `/api`, `/assets`, `/.well-known`, `/_serverFn`,
  `/serwist` and `verify-token`, so open tabs, API clients, uploads and auth
  return URLs on the subdomain keep working.
- An unlisted app is served through its binding without redirecting, so the
  hostname can be attached before the redirect is switched on.

The `301` carries `Cache-Control: no-store`, so browsers do not keep it:
a rollback takes effect on the next request, and a later fetch or webhook
retry to a redirected URL still reaches the app.

Rollback: remove the app from `SUBDOMAIN_REDIRECT_APPS`, or reattach the
hostname to the app Worker from the capture. Regression coverage lives in
`apps/gateway/src/subdomain-redirect.test.ts`.

## Web route families

Route families of `apps/web` built as their own Worker (see
[Web route families on Cloudflare](/build/devops/web-opennext-families)) are
reached through gateway service bindings on the existing `tuturuuu.com/*`
route. Family Workers have no routes, so no zone or DNS change is involved.

- `webFamilies` in `apps/gateway/src/manifest.json` lists each family: `id`,
  `binding` (`WEB_FAMILY_<ID>`), `exact` paths, raw `prefix` entries (each
  ending in `/`), `exclude` subtrees, `localized` and `assetPrefix` (`/_f/<id>`
  for page families, stripped before the family sees the request). Matching is
  method-agnostic.
- `webFamilies.deny` lists subtrees that never reach an OpenNext family,
  whatever the flags say; the vinext table assigns them to `api-ops`, and
  without it they go to `web-rest`: `/api/v1/auth/accounts`, `/api/cron`,
  `/api/notifications/send-immediate`, `/api/v1/infrastructure`,
  `/api/v1/devboxes`, the ChatGPT credential routes and `/_next/image`.
- `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` (comma-separated ids, default empty) turns families
  on. A listed family serves its paths only when its binding exists;
  otherwise they go to the fallback family `web-rest`.

Order in the handler: loop check, mounts, Marketing origin paths (cached),
then the vinext route table, the OpenNext deny list and first flagged, bound
family, then the bound fallback `web-rest`. `web-rest` needs only its binding,
not a flag. Without it the request answers `503`. Families do not apply the signed-in/RSC/server-action bypass:
those requests are what moves.

The family request keeps method, body, query, cookies, `authorization` and
`cf-connecting-ip`. Client forwarding headers (the list in the mounted-app
section) are stripped, and the gateway sets `x-forwarded-host: PUBLIC_HOST`,
`x-forwarded-proto: https` and `x-gateway-hop: 1`. Next's server-action origin
check relies on this contract. Responses carry `x-gateway-cache: FAMILY` and
`x-gateway-family: <id>`, are never stored in the gateway cache, and keep
`Set-Cookie` and `cache-control` as the family sent them. A throwing binding
answers `502 gateway family unreachable`.

Security header parity: the gateway fills `Strict-Transport-Security:
max-age=63072000` and `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` on family responses that
lack them. It never overrides a header the
family sends (CSP, `X-Frame-Options`, route-specific `Referrer-Policy`) and
adds no `Permissions-Policy`, which the live responses do not carry. The other
live security headers (`X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-XSS-Protection`,
`Expect-CT`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`) match the zone's "Add security
headers" managed transform and appear on every gateway response today; the
per-family S3 header diff confirms them on family responses. Regression coverage
lives in `apps/gateway/src/web-family.test.ts`.

**Rollback** is the previous gateway version, or the family's previous Worker
version. Enabling a family is a change of the
`GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` repository variable followed by a run of the gateway job,
which adds the family's service binding.

### vinext family route table

The vinext family Workers (`tuturuuu-web-vinext-<id>`, see
[Web vinext Workers](/build/devops/web-vinext-families)) are routed from
`apps/gateway/src/web-routes.generated.json`. It is generated from the app
route entries and `apps/web/cloudflare/vinext/families.json` by
`bun run --cwd apps/web routes:gateway`; a test fails when it is stale.

- Each app route entry is a pattern owned by one family. The gateway picks the
  most specific matching pattern as Next.js does (static segments over
  `[param]` over `[...rest]` over `[[...rest]]`), with an optional leading
  locale for localized routes. Unlisted paths under a family's prefixes stay
  with that family (an unknown first segment is a workspace slug, so it goes
  to `dashboard`). Framework endpoints (`/_next/image`, `/_vinext/*`),
  doubled slashes and backslashes go to the catch-all family `web-rest`.
  Unprefixed `/_next/static/*` and `/_f/<id>/` paths of non-vinext builders
  never reach a vinext family: only pages rendered elsewhere emit them, so they
  keep their own route.
- `api-ops` owns the OpenNext deny list paths, including the ChatGPT
  credential routes.
- Each page family serves its own client assets under `/_f/<id>/`. The path
  reaches the family unchanged, and the family serves it from its own assets.
- A family takes traffic only when its id is in `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` and
  `WEB_FAMILY_<ID>` is bound; otherwise its paths fall through to the OpenNext
  families and then the bound `web-rest` fallback. The vinext table runs before the OpenNext table, after mounts,
  and not for paths the manifest sends to another configured origin (marketing
  assets and flagged marketing groups).
- Cross-family client navigation is a hard navigation: every family build has
  its own RSC compatibility id, and vinext reloads the page when a response's
  id differs.

Bindings: `WEB_FAMILY_API_OPS`, `WEB_FAMILY_API_CORE`,
`WEB_FAMILY_PUBLIC_AUTH`, `WEB_FAMILY_DASHBOARD_APPS`, `WEB_FAMILY_DASHBOARD`,
`WEB_FAMILY_WEB_REST`. `scripts/ci/gateway-deploy-config.mjs` admits a vinext
id in `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` only when `families.json` marks it `activated`.
Page families activate after a build with their `/_f/<id>` asset prefix.

All six families are activated and flagged
(`GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES=public-docs,api-ops,api-core,public-auth,web-rest,dashboard-apps,dashboard`).
Unprefixed `/_next/static/*` and `/_f/<id>/*` for an id no Worker builds go
to `web-rest`; requests for another host get `503`.

**Uploading a gateway version** (no traffic until it is deployed), from a
clean checkout at a commit on `main`:

```bash
node scripts/ci/gateway-deploy-config.mjs capture settings.json   # serving version's bindings
WEB_ORIGIN=<live value> MARKETING_ORIGIN=<live value> GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES=<ids> \
  node scripts/ci/gateway-deploy-config.mjs write settings.json apps/gateway/wrangler.deploy.json
cd apps/gateway && wrangler versions upload --config wrangler.deploy.json \
  --tag <sha10> --message "<what changes>"
```

`capture` reads the version that serves traffic (`/deployments`, then
`/versions/<id>`), never `/settings`, and `write` keeps its mounts, services
and variables while adding the flagged family bindings. A version upload
inherits the serving version's secrets, so it needs no `--secrets-file` once
`TRUSTED_PROXY_ORIGIN_SECRET` is live. Read the version back
(`GET .../workers/scripts/tuturuuu-gateway/versions/<id>`) and diff its
binding names against the capture before handing it over.

**Cutover:** deploy the uploaded version at 0%, then smoke with
`Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides: tuturuuu-gateway="<version id>"`. Each
moved path answers with `x-gateway-family: <id>`, and each family serves one
of its `/_f/<id>/_next/static/*` assets. Then move the version to 100%.
**Rollback:** re-assign the previous gateway version. A broken family Worker
rolls back to its own previous Worker version instead (see
[Web vinext Workers](/build/devops/web-vinext-families#deploying-a-family)).
Dropping an id from `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` sends its paths to `web-rest`,
which does not own them, so it is not a rollback.

## Path ownership and rollback

Each gateway path has one owner. Alias collisions are rejected at manifest
validation. A one-action rollback restores all affected surfaces, including
bare-query fallback paths. Mounted app traffic bypasses the gateway cache and
forwarding headers are stripped.
